Sri Venkata Raghava Surendra Muvvala vs The State Of Andhra
Pradesh on 7 February, 2022
Author: Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
Bench: Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE CHEEKATI MANAVENDRANATH ROY
 CRIMINAL PETITION NOS.480, 485, 488 AND 489 OF 2022
COMMON ORDER:
-
These criminal petitions under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, are filed
seeking quash of F.I.Rs in Crime No.7 of 2022 of Martur Police Station, Prakasam District registered
for the offences punishable under Sections 20(2), 24(1) r/w 6(A) r/w 7(1) r/w 8(1)(a) r/w 10 of the
Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and
Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (for short "COTP Act"); Crime No.14 of
2022 of Ongole I Town Police Station, Prakasam District registered for the offences punishable
under Section 272 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "I.P.C."), under Section 20(2) and 24(1)
of the COTP Act and under Section 55 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short "F.S.S.
Act") and Crime No.12 of 2022 of Sattenapalli Town Police Station, Guntur District registered for
the offences punishable under Sections 420, 188, 272, 273 of I.P.C. and under Section 20(1) r/w 7(1)
of the COTP Act and charge sheet in C.C.No.2721 of 2019 on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate of
First Class, Nandyal filed for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 273, 328 r/w 34 of I.P.C.
and under Section 59(i) of F.S.S. Act, respectively.
2. Heard learned counsel for petitioners and the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.
3. These are covered matters in view of the earlier common orders passed by this Court in Criminal
Petition No.5421 of 2019 and batch and in Criminal Petition Nos.2966 of 2021 and batch, whereby
this Court has quashed several F.I.Rs registered for the similar offences based on identical facts.
Therefore, the petitioners, who are similarly placed, are also entitled for quash of the F.I.Rs and
charge sheet registered against them.
4. Therefore, in view of the aforesaid common orders of this Court and for the reasons stated
therein, these Criminal Petitions are allowed and the aforesaid F.I.Rs and charge sheet registered
against the petitioners, are hereby quashed.
Miscellaneous Petitions, if any pending, in these Criminal Petitions, shall stand closed.
Sri Venkata Raghava Surendra Muvvala vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 7 February, 2022

texts.arguments_petitioner: Petitioner argues for the quashing of FIRs under Section 482 of CrPC, citing procedural irregularities and lack of evidence.
texts.arguments_respondent: Respondent argues against the quashing of FIRs, emphasizing the seriousness of the offences and the need for investigation.
texts.reasoning_text: The Court considers the jurisdiction and applicability of Section 482 of CrPC, the interpretation of provisions under the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act, and the procedural compliance in registering FIRs.
texts.decision_text: The Court grants the petition and quashes the FIRs.
